research_rationale: Executive Order 6744-A (June 19, 1934) approves the Code of Fair Competition for the Retail Tobacco Trade under Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act. The held text is the American Presidency Project transcription (grade mirror_transcription, acceptable_as_original false; Common Crawl capture 2025-05-18T23:19:44Z); the standing note applies: original not yet held; replace and re-check quotes when an official copy is retrieved. The order approves the code effective June 19, 1934 with five conditions: two stays that end on June 25, 1934 by their own terms, two stays with contingent ends, and substituted pricing standards. Because each command is dependent on the code and no held record shows an earlier end, the first end is the statutory repeal of the code approval and enforcement provisions by section 2 of S.J. Res. 113, effective June 14, 1935. Schechter, decided May 27, 1935, held the section 3 delegation unconstitutional; that is recorded as a validity characterization (void from issuance under then-prevailing doctrine), not as an end date, because the judgment cancelled no approval. The antitrust-exemption proviso of the resolution is not settled by the held text for past action; whatever survives is an accrued effect, not continued operation of the approval.
